title: Beef Goulash
subtitle: Slow-braised beef in a paprika-rich sauce
excerpt: Chunks of beef chuck braised low and slow with sweet and smoked paprika, peppers, and tomatoes until falling tender. Served with soured cream, this is a warming, deeply flavoured dish that freezes well.
sourceNotes: Goulash originated with Hungarian cattle herders who dried spiced meat for preservation. The dish became a national symbol of Hungary in the 18th century during a period of national revival. Versions spread widely across Central Europe, with German goulash typically being slightly milder and richer with the addition of soured cream.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze the goulash without the soured cream. Reheat gently on the hob and stir in soured cream just before serving.
recipe.batchNotes: This recipe doubles well. Use a large stockpot and extend the browning time.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Like most braises, this tastes better the next day.

content.text: Do not rush the onions. Cooking them low and slow for a full 20 minutes until very soft and sweet forms the base of the sauce and is what gives goulash its characteristic body.
Season the beef generously. Heat the oil in a stockpot over high heat and brown the beef in batches for 2 to 3 minutes per batch, turning once. Remove and set aside.
Reduce the heat to low and add the onions. Cook for 18 to 20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until very soft and starting to colour. Add the garlic and cook for 1 more minute.
Stir in both paprikas and the fennel seeds. Cook for 1 minute. Add the tomato puree and cook for another minute. Add the red peppers, tinned tomatoes, and beef stock.

Return the browned beef to the pot. Bring to a simmer, cover with a lid, and cook on very low heat for 1 hour 30 minutes to 2 hours until the beef is very tender. Stir occasionally and add a splash of water if it looks dry.
Remove the lid for the last 15 minutes to thicken the sauce. Season to taste and serve with soured cream swirled through.

items.symptom: Beef is still tough after 2 hours
items.cause: Heat was too high or pieces too large
items.fix: Keep the heat very low and check pieces are no larger than 4 cm.

items.cause: Paprika was added to a dry, overheated pan
items.fix: Always add paprika with some moisture or fat in the pan.

items.cause: Lid was kept on for the full cook time
items.fix: Remove the lid for the last 15 to 20 minutes to reduce it.
